families.source: UKHSA national measles case and contact management guidelines
families.topic: suspected case assessment, notification, testing, contact risk and post-exposure prophylaxis
evidence_points: The national guidelines support management of suspected measles cases.
They specify patient information needed for public-health assessment and notification.
They provide a framework for assessing whether a suspected case is likely or unlikely.
They describe laboratory investigation and the importance of oral-fluid testing for suspected cases.
They cover identification of vulnerable contacts.
They support assessment of post-exposure prophylaxis needs.
The page provides warn-and-inform letters and translated resources.
The guidance was updated to version 7 in April 2026.
A suspected clinical presentation is not equivalent to laboratory confirmation.
PEP and contact action require current timing, susceptibility, exposure and risk-group evidence.

families.source: UKHSA management guidance for scabies cases and outbreaks in communal residential settings
families.topic: case diagnosis, contact treatment, outbreak control, PPE, cleaning and movement risk
families.page_title: Management of scabies cases and outbreaks in communal residential settings
evidence_points: The guidance is for health protection teams, community teams and managers of communal residential settings.
Covered settings include care homes, boarding schools, children's homes, prisons, detention settings, asylum accommodation and hostels.
Diagnosed cases should receive treatment promptly rather than waiting for wider setting treatment.
Close contacts may need identification across the 8 weeks before diagnosis.
Two or more epidemiologically linked cases within 8 weeks constitute an outbreak in the guidance.
Coordinated treatment of cases and contacts is used to break transmission.
Control measures include PPE, laundry management and environmental cleaning.
Transfers, admissions and movements should be risk assessed during case and outbreak management.
UKHSA does not provide the individual clinical diagnosis, and persistent itching alone does not prove active infestation.
Symptoms can persist after treatment, so treatment failure requires clinical review and evidence rather than itching alone.

families.source: UKHSA and NHS England management guidance for tuberculosis in secure settings
families.topic: TB prevention, diagnosis, notification, case management and outbreak control in secure settings
families.page_title: Management of tuberculosis in secure settings in England
evidence_points: The guidance supports prevention, diagnosis and management of tuberculosis in secure settings in England.
It uses a multiagency approach involving UKHSA, NHS England and justice or detention partners.
Covered settings include adult prisons, young offender institutions, approved premises and immigration removal settings.
It addresses detection and management of TB cases.
It specifies notification and coordination with relevant stakeholders.
It includes incident and outbreak management.
It covers prevention of additional cases among residents and staff.
The 2025 to 2026 guidance combines earlier prison-healthcare and health-protection guidance.
Secure-setting exposure or residence alone does not establish active or latent TB.
Screening, diagnosis and management require current clinical, microbiological, radiological and specialist TB evidence.

families.source: UKHSA CJD public health action guidance for new cases and people at increased risk
families.topic: CJD incident assessment, follow-up, surveillance and infection-control response
families.page_title: CJD: public health action following report of new case or person at increased risk
evidence_points: The guidance addresses public-health follow-up after a newly diagnosed or suspected CJD case is reported.
It also addresses a person identified as being at increased risk of CJD.
It covers surgical procedures where transmissible spongiform encephalopathy infection-control guidance was not followed.
Local trusts, hospitals and health protection teams are responsible for incident investigation and management.
The publication is intended for trusts, hospitals, health protection teams and health boards.
It provides investigation and enhanced-surveillance forms.
Incident assessment includes the relevant procedure, instruments, patient pathway and infection-control evidence.
The content is owned and managed by UKHSA.
Being classified at increased risk is not the same as a clinical diagnosis of CJD.
Public-health action requires incident-specific assessment and current specialist CJD and infection-control advice.
